dataFlow: The merchant creates a bundle (fixed or flexible) from the admin panel, which persists the bundle definition and its discount tiers to the database and simultaneously provisions a Shopify product bundle and one discount code per tier in Shopify. When a customer visits a product page, the storefront widget fetches the bundle definition(s) for that product; the customer picks their items (for flexible bundles), sees a live discounted total, and clicks "Add bundle to cart" — the widget calls the backend which adds all variant lines to the Shopify cart and applies the matching tier discount code. When an order is paid, the backend matches any applied bundle discount code to its bundle definition, records a purchase attribution row, and increments the bundle's purchase count snapshot. When a product or variant is updated or deleted in Shopify, the backend marks any bundle that references that product or variant as degraded and surfaces a warning in the admin panel so the merchant can take corrective action.

triggers.idempotency: process the latest payload state; repeated deliveries for the same product are safe because the handler re-evaluates all bundles referencing the product and writes the current degraded state, making the operation idempotent

edgeCases: Duplicate orders/paid webhook delivery for the same order — the handler checks for an existing attribution row by order external id and exits before any write if one is found.
Duplicate products/update webhook delivery for the same product — the handler re-evaluates and re-writes the current degraded state idempotently; no side effect fires twice.

Customer adds the same bundle to the cart a second time — the widget detects the bundle's discount code is already applied to the cart and warns the customer that a second discount will not stack; the cart lines are still added but no second discount code is applied.

A component product is deleted mid-campaign (products/delete fires) — the bundle is flagged as degraded and the widget suppresses it from the storefront; the admin panel surfaces a prominent warning with the affected bundle name.

Flexible bundle: customer submits fewer items than the required pick count — the backend rejects the add-to-cart request and returns a validation error; the widget renders an inline item-count indicator.

Shopify discount code creation fails for any tier during bundle provisioning — the entire bundle create is rolled back in the database; the merchant sees an error in the admin UI and no partially-provisioned bundle record is left behind.

A tier's discount code becomes unreachable at cart application time — the backend surfaces a recoverable warning to the widget and prompts the merchant via admin to re-sync the bundle's discount codes.
